L143: The radial map realizes equality. This is the key point of the framework adopted in this paper: the conjecture is exactly what the canonical one-mode examples suggest. The proposed equality case in [【25†11】] is radial, and the principal harmonic maps and equality cases appearing there are also one-mode maps. Thus, the conjecture was natural precisely, because every such model points to the same expression.
L145: The failure of the radial bound suggests a more natural extremal problem. For $1<s<S$, let $\mathcal{H}(s,S)$ denote the class of harmonic orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms from $A(1,s)$ onto $A(1,S)$. Put
L146: 
L147:  | $$\mathcal{H}_{qc}(s,S)=\{h\in\mathcal{H}(s,S):\|\omega_{h}\|_{\infty}<1\}$$  |
L148: 
L149: and define
L150: 
L151:  | $$q_{*}(s,S)=\inf_{h\in\mathcal{H}_{qc}(s,S)}\|\omega_{h}\|_{\infty},\qquad K_{*}(s,S)=\frac{1+q_{*}(s,S)}{1-q_{*}(s,S)}.$$  |
L152: The radial upper model gives the value $\kappa(s,S)$, whereas Theorem 【49†3.3】 gives $q_{*}(s,S)<\kappa(s,S)$. Thus, any genuine harmonic quasiconformal extremal attaining $q_{*}(s,S)$, if such an extremal exists, must be non-radial. Describing such extremal maps and their minimal-surface lifts is the natural replacement for the original radial conjecture.
L153: ###### Remark 1.2 (The range $S\leq s$).
L154: 
L155: The upper estimate (【50†2】) is automatic when $S\leq s$, because
L156: 
L157:  | $$\Phi_{K}(s)-s=\frac{K-1}{2}\left(s-\frac{1}{s}\right)\geq 0.$$  |
L158: 
L159: However, for $S<s$ harmonic diffeomorphisms do not exist for all parameters. The Nitsche conjecture, proved by Iwaniec–Kovalev–Onninen [【35†10】], says that a harmonic homeomorphism $A(1,s)\to A(1,S)$ can exist only if
L160: 
L161:  | $$S\geq\frac{1}{2}\left(s+\frac{1}{s}\right),$$  |
L162: and this bound is sharp. Hence the genuinely restrictive part of [【25†11】, Conjecture 1.8] lies in the thickening range $1<s<S$.
L163: We close the introduction by describing the organization of the paper. Section 【7†2】 recalls the radial equality model and fixes the normalization against which the later constructions are measured. Section 【8†3】 proves the main negative result by constructing, for each pair $1<s<S$, a high-frequency non-radial harmonic diffeomorphism whose maximal complex dilatation is strictly below the conjectural threshold.
L164: Section 【9†4】 isolates several regimes, in which the one-mode mechanism still forces the conjectured estimate, including an inner-boundary energy criterion, a Fourier spectral criterion, and a low-frequency stability theorem. Section 【14†5】 develops the minimal-surface interpretation: the lift criterion, the slope formula, the catenoidal/helicoidal sign distinction, the vertical-periodic lift of the counterexamples, and a perturbative zero-period theorem for single-valued minimal graphs.
